mission: Day four in hyperspace. The ship smells like six people in a space for two. Desh keeps an ironic tally of arguments on his datapad. Kael laughs for the first time anyone has heard — short, genuine, cut off. The whole ship notices. Per D7 counter-current 2: in the galley's low-grade philosophical sparring, an opening arises where Torin could naturally pull Kael toward the technique-as-correction line (Kael's institutional-skeptic register would be receptive; the recruitment cost would be minimal). Torin declines — a small redirection of the conversation away from Kael, unframed, uncommented on. Kael notices. Ben notices Kael noticing. Neither interprets it.
why_now: Breathing room between nodes. The Kael/Desh warmth needs one more visible beat before the midpoint, and Ben and Desh both need the cockpit-door to close on them before Scene 2 can happen. The D7 counter-current places here because Kael's laugh has opened a window of communal warmth that a corruption-trajectory Torin would exploit; this Torin does not.
conflict: Low-level friction from overcrowding. Sera's formality grates against Desh's casualness. Torin's warmth lands on its beats slightly too cleanly — the first time anyone might register the timing as a rhythm rather than a person. Inside that texture, Torin's small refusal to recruit Kael reads as a real ambiguity: a man on the corruption trajectory would take the free pitch; this one does not.
turning_point: Kael laughs. A short, genuine sound, cut short the way Kael cuts everything. The whole ship notices without saying so.
opening_hook: Day four in hyperspace. The ship smells like six people who've been living in a space designed for two. Desh has started keeping score of arguments
closing_hook: Desh catches Ben alone in the cockpit. 'Can we talk about something that isn't the Force?' His voice is too casual. Whatever he wants to discuss, he's been working up to it
emotional_trajectory: Cramped humor -> interpersonal warmth (Kael's laugh) -> Torin's small refusal -> Desh's deliberate opening

On the corruption trajectory, Torin would want Kael in his camp (Kael's institutional-skepticism register is naturally receptive to the technique-as-correction argument); here he passes on the opportunity. The beat must read as characterisation, not plot signal — Ben files the mis-fit the way he files the smell of the ship; analysis belongs to later chapters. Per D7 anti-pattern, narrator does not correct Ben's file-and-move-on; no 'Torin was sparing Kael for reasons Ben would only later understand' line. Hold the beat as live ambiguity. key_beats.beat_description: Desh marks another tally on his datapad as Sera and Torin disagree about galley rotation. The argument is low-level, but the tally makes it concrete.
key_beats.state_change: Abstract cramping becomes observable friction. The ship's resource constraints (two-person design, six occupants) surface in a specific disagreement about space and routine.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben registers the pressure as something that pushes toward action rather than explanation — a physical restlessness, an instinct to move or solve rather than sit with discomfort. The cramped air itself becomes a sensory anchor for his awareness.

key_beats.beat_description: Kael laughs at something Desh says — a short, genuine sound that stops every conversation on the ship. It is over before anyone can turn around.
key_beats.state_change: Pressure inverts from friction to warmth. Kael has allowed himself a fraction of company, and the group registers it without comment. The laugh is the first genuine one anyone has heard from him.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's focus tightens on what just changed. The laugh arrives as a small permission — Kael lowering a guard just enough to let sound out. Ben feels the shift in the room's temperature, the way everyone's attention pivots toward Kael without anyone moving.

key_beats.beat_description: In the galley's low-grade philosophical sparring about the technique and correction, an opening surfaces where Torin could naturally draw Kael into the argument. Kael's institutional-skeptic register would be receptive; the recruitment cost would be minimal. Torin does not take it. The conversation moves elsewhere. Kael's eyes flick once to Torin and back to Desh.
key_beats.state_change: Torin's warmth becomes slightly mechanical — his refusal surfaces within the warmth, not against it. The timing of his story-telling and his pivot away from Kael arrives just a little too cleanly. Ben files the mis-fit the way he files the smell of the ship: noted, not analyzed.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben observes Kael's eye-flick to Torin and back to Desh without interpreting it. He does not articulate 'Torin's warmth is becoming a performance.' Instead, he registers the rhythm of Torin's warmth as slightly off-beat, the way a musician notices a note played slightly flat. The ambiguity lodges in Ben's filing system: Torin passed on a free pitch. Ben does not yet know why.

key_beats.beat_description: Desh drops into the co-pilot seat beside Ben with studied casualness and waits until the cockpit door closes behind them.
key_beats.state_change: The scene isolates Ben and Desh from the group. The cockpit door closing signals a boundary — whatever Desh wants to discuss, it is separate from the galley's warmth and friction.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben feels the shift in Desh's deliberateness. The casualness is a performance, and Ben recognizes it as such. He braces for the handoff: Desh has been working up to something that is not about the Force, and the door closing is the signal that the conversation is about to begin.
